title: Open Source security in spite of AI - Daniel Stenberg
summary: curl's Daniel Stenberg at FOSDEM: AI slop security reports swamp maintainers, while AI analyzers and reviewers find real bugs.

assertions.quote: We used to have one in six reports were genuine ... now it's more like one in 20 or one in 30

verdicts.note: curl's public data and statements from other maintainers (Python, Django, FFmpeg) document a sharp rise in fabricated AI reports; curl ended its bug bounty in 2026 partly because of it.

assertions.quote: I have fixed more than 100 bugs found by these tools when I started to use them

verdicts.note: AI reviewers do catch real defects missed by humans, though with notable false-positive rates; complement, not replacement.

assertions.quote: they're certainly not a compliment to test cases ... test cases is still way more important

verdicts.note: AI reviewers miss many defects that tests catch and are nondeterministic; tests remain the reliable regression check. Consistent with curl experience and review-tool benchmarks.

assertions.quote: All of these AI detection tools ... offer like generate a patch to fix this, but they're never good

verdicts.note: Maintainers widely report poor auto-fixes, and fix quality lags detection in evaluations; but auto-fix quality has improved and varies by bug type.

assertions.quote: they easily swallow 75 terabytes per month ... less than 0.01% of the traffic [is downloads]

verdicts.note: Many projects (SourceHut, GNOME, KDE, Fedora, Read the Docs) reported AI-scraper traffic overwhelming servers in 2025 and deployed blockers like Anubis.
